blocks.content: Course: Rapid Build With Claude Code

Every page in SpeedBlip lives inside the navigation shell. The AppLayout component wraps every app route, renders the sidebar or bottom nav based on screen width, and provides the main content area where each page renders.

If you build pages before the navigation shell, one of two things happens: either every page has its own layout code that you later have to extract and centralize, or you build pages that look correct in isolation but break when the layout wraps them.
Navigation first is the right order because:

items: It defines the available space for every page (sidebar width, content padding, bottom nav height)
It establishes the route configuration once, in one place
It gives Claude Code a complete AppLayout wrapper to use in every subsequent page chunk

blocks.content: For SpeedBlip, Chunk 2a built the entire navigation system before a single page existed. By the time Chunk 4 built the Dashboard, there was already a production-quality layout wrapper waiting for it.
